chunks: From him, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a tooth and an arm that are broken intentionally: is there indemnity for them, or retaliation? He said: "Retaliation." He said: I said: then if they satisfy him with whatever he wishes, it is his.

key_terms.أَرْشٌ: financial indemnity or assessed compensation for injury
key_terms.أَرْضَوْهُ: they satisfy him or reach his approval through settlement
key_terms.الذِّرَاعِ: the arm, as an injured limb in the ruling
key_terms.السِّنِّ: the tooth, as an injured body part in the ruling
key_terms.بِمَا شَاءَ: with whatever he wishes, meaning an agreed amount or form of compensation
key_terms.قَوَدٌ: retaliatory retribution in cases of intentional bodily injury

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia fiqh for intentionally breaking a tooth or an arm: indemnity or retaliation?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling for intentionally breaking a tooth or an arm. The Imam عليه السلام states that the ruling is qawad (retaliatory retribution), but if the injured party accepts a mutually agreed compensation, then that settlement belongs to him.
